findings.title: Grant shortcuts must be fixed at two characters
findings.body: The parser requires the encoded context to be exactly six characters and slices the grant shortcut as two characters, but `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` documents shortcuts as “usually” three letters, without requiring a two-character value. A custom grant using a documented three-character shortcut can be encoded, but its token ID will fail to parse. Require and validate exactly two characters in the factory contract, or make the encoding and parser support variable-length shortcuts.

findings.title: Access-token event matcher does not verify the grant shortcut
findings.body: This condition returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut, and the extraction uses `substring(3, 5)` rather than the grant shortcut's positions 4–5. For normal IDs such as `onrtac:<uuid>`, it therefore ignores the grant and accepts IDs with the wrong grant shortcut, so the updated integration assertions cannot catch mis-tagged tokens.

findings.title: The constructor does not reject a null raw token ID
findings.body: This second null check checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. A context with a null raw ID is accepted, and encoding it appends the literal string `null` to the token ID rather than rejecting invalid input.
